newsitem.title: MALI: Six held in Mali over lynching of policeman.
newsitem.headline: Six held in Mali over lynching of policeman.

text.p: Six opposition leaders were detained in the Mali capital Bamako on Monday after their arrest over the lynching of a policeman, political sources said.
The policeman was beaten to death when he was set upon on Saturday at a rally of an alliance of 18 opposition parties disputing the conduct of a presidential election in May.
The detained men are accused of incitement but no charges have been brought against them, opposition officials said.
Police mounted a search of districts of the capital on Saturday and Sunday nights when they arrested the six, among them opposition alliance president Almamy Sylla.
Recent political violence in Mali has seriously dented the former French colony's image as a model democracy after a successful 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship.
The radical opposition boycotted parliamentary polls in July as part of a campaign to force President Alpha Oumar Konare to scrap and reschedule this year's second multi-party elections.
Two people were killed in unrest.
Saturday's violence followed a meeting between Konare and opposition leaders to try and defuse the political crisis.
